group_structure: HSBC's GCC business runs mainly through HSBC Bank Middle East Limited (HBME), a DIFC company with branches and subsidiaries across the Middle East and North Africa: the UAE branch (HBME UAE Operations, CBUAE-regulated, separately reported in AED), Qatar and other Middle East branches, and an Oman wholesale-only branch opened 2024. HBME reports two segments: Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB) and International Wealth and Premier Banking (IWPB = Premier, Private Bank and asset-management manufacturing). Separately within HSBC Group: HSBC Private Bank (Suisse) SA DIFC branch; HSBC Asset Management's UAE (Dubai) business with onshore SCA-registered funds (Jan 2026); in Saudi Arabia, a 51% stake in HSBC Saudi Arabia (investment bank; SAB holds 49%), a 31% stake in Saudi Awwal Bank (SAB, profiled separately as sa-sab), and HSBC Capital RHQ (MISA regional HQ licence, Dec 2025). Double counting: HBME UAE Operations figures are included in HBME consolidated figures; SAB is an associate of HSBC and is not consolidated in HBME - do not add SAB's figures to this profile. HSBC presence in MENAT: nine countries (Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, UAE).

capabilities.wealth_summary: HSBC's GCC wealth business sits in the International Wealth and Premier Banking (IWPB) segment of HSBC Bank Middle East (H1 2026 IWPB income USD 408m, PBT USD 109m), led regionally by Dinesh Sharma. In Sep 2025 HSBC called its UAE push its biggest IWPB investment in two decades: the first Middle East wealth centre (Jumeirah, Dubai, for Premier and HNW clients), a revamped Premier account (AED 500k relationship balance) with an in-app Future Planner tool (Oct 2025), and a doubling of affluent frontline staff. Self-directed investing runs on WorldTrader, powered by Interactive Brokers (U.K.) Limited, offering ADX/DFM and international stocks, ETFs, funds and bonds (USD 800m traded in its first 12 months). In Jan 2026 HSBC Asset Management opened a Dubai branch and registered 10 onshore SCA feeder funds, including World Selection multi-asset portfolios and three Shariah/sukuk funds. HSBC Private Bank (MENA head Aladdin Hangari; UAE head Feras Al Jarmani from Aug 2026) operates from the DIFC and aims to be the leading private bank in the region.

HSBC AM global AUM USD 852bn (Sep 2025).

initiatives.what: HSBC Private Bank unified UAE private banking teams under Feras Al Jarmani; stated ambition to be the leading private bank in the Middle East.
Launched Tokenised Deposit Service in the UAE for corporate liquidity (24/7 on-chain transfers).
HSBC Asset Management launched UAE onshore business (Dubai branch) and 10 SCA-registered funds.
MISA granted HSBC a Regional HQ licence for Capital Markets and Advisory in Saudi Arabia (HSBC Capital RHQ).
Revamped Premier account in the UAE with Future Planner planning tool in the mobile app.
Opened first Middle East wealth centre (Jumeirah, Dubai); described as HSBC's biggest IWPB investment in two decades.
Named Elie El Asmar CEO of new wholesale-only Oman branch (opening May 2024).

opportunities: States its UAE wealth push is its biggest IWPB investment in 20 years, with the goal of being the UAE's leading international wealth player (S8, S14).
No discretionary, model-portfolio or private-markets offering found on UAE pages; HBME DFSA licence lacks managing assets (S17, S18).
Shift to onshore, UAE-domiciled products (10 SCA funds launched Jan 2026) (S9).
barriers: WorldTrader execution and custody already outsourced to Interactive Brokers (U.K.) Limited (S15).
In-house manufacturing via HSBC Asset Management, including Shariah funds (S9).
Group-wide propositions (Premier revamp and Future Planner rolled out globally) suggest group-level platform decisions (S10).
